Jenkins

Jenkins jobs, builds, console logs and triggering builds, on one or more named instances

skills/toil/jenkins.md

Jobs, builds, console logs and the build queue on Jenkins, through its classic remote access API (/api/json with tree, consoleText, /queue/item). Every command reads except pipeline run, which triggers a build. Verification level: unit.

Supported versions: The oldest Jenkins version toil supports hasn’t been established. toil calls the classic remote access API with a user name and API token sent as Basic auth. No release has been verified yet.

Credential

A Jenkins API token and the user name it belongs to: in Jenkins, your user name → Security → API Token → Add new token. toil sends Authorization: Basic base64(username:apiToken); both parts are required. No CSRF crumb is requested, and there is no password or browser login.

Configuration

KeyEnv varRequiredMeaning
baseUrlTOIL_JENKINS_BASE_URLyesJenkins server root, e.g. https://jenkins.imagile.dev (keep any context path)
usernameTOIL_JENKINS_USERNAMEyesJenkins user name the API token belongs to
apiTokenTOIL_JENKINS_API_TOKENyesJenkins API token
instanceTOIL_JENKINS_INSTANCEnoThe name --instance selects this connection by, when it isn’t the connection’s own name

There’s no CI fallback variable. Environment variables (CI, or a one-off shell) configure the default connection:

export TOIL_JENKINS_BASE_URL=https://jenkins.imagile.dev
export TOIL_JENKINS_USERNAME=ci-bot
export TOIL_JENKINS_API_TOKEN=<your API token>

Named instances

Each Jenkins server is its own connection. --instance <name> (on the group: toil jenkins --instance ephemeral pipeline list, or the instance field over MCP) selects the jenkins connection with that name, or the one whose instance setting is that name. An unknown name is INVALID_INPUT, listing the ones toil knows. Without --instance, the area’s default connection is used.

{
  "version": 2,
  "connections": {
    "jenkins": { "area": "jenkins", "baseUrl": "https://jenkins.imagile.dev", "username": "ci-bot" },
    "ephemeral": { "area": "jenkins", "baseUrl": "https://jenkins-tmp.imagile.dev", "username": "tmp-user" }
  },
  "defaults": { "jenkins": { "connection": "jenkins" } }
}

The API token never goes in this file; a plaintext one there is refused with CONFIG_INVALID. Add an instance with toil connections add ephemeral --area jenkins, which asks for each setting and keeps the token in the OS credential store; remove one with toil connections remove ephemeral. In CI, define one with TOIL_CONN_EPHEMERAL_AREA=jenkins and TOIL_CONN_EPHEMERAL_BASE_URL, _USERNAME and _API_TOKEN.

  • instance list: List configured Jenkins instances. It is toil connections list --area jenkins: every jenkins connection’s name, host, whether it’s the default, whether writes are on, and where each setting came from, never a secret. Over MCP, call connections_list with area: "jenkins".
  • instance add <name>: CLI only. It is toil connections add <name> --area jenkins, asking for each setting on a terminal and keeping the token in the OS credential store. It takes the name as an argument and accepts none of the contract’s --name, --base-url, --username, --api-token and --force flags.
  • instance remove <name>: CLI only. It is toil connections remove <name> --area jenkins, which also deletes the token from the OS credential store and refuses a connection to another area. It takes the name as an argument, not --name.

Commands

Job names with folders are written folder/job (platform/api-build); each level becomes /job/<segment>, percent-encoded.

  • pipeline list: List all jobs on the Jenkins instance (or within a folder, --folder parent/child).
  • pipeline get: Get details for a specific job (--name), with its last 10 builds.
  • pipeline run: Trigger a build (--name). It writes, so it needs writes: true on the connection and --allow-write. Each --parameter key=value (repeatable) sends the build to buildWithParameters; without one it goes to build, even for a parameterized job. Without --wait, data is { queueItemId }. With --wait it polls every --poll seconds (default 10) until the build leaves the queue, then until it finishes, giving each phase --timeout seconds (default 600), and returns the build. A build whose result is set and isn’t SUCCESS is still returned as data with ok: true, but the CLI exits 1, and meta.warnings has a JENKINS_BUILD_NOT_SUCCESSFUL warning (over MCP, check the warning or data.result). The command’s time limit is 21 minutes (TOIL_TIMEOUT_MS overrides it). --timeout and --poll are checked only after the build was triggered.
  • pipeline list-runs: List recent builds for a job (--name, --top, default 25). Jenkins’ builds list holds only the newest 100.
  • pipeline get-run: Get details for a specific build (--name, --number).
  • pipeline logs: Fetch console log for a build (consider —output-file for large logs); data is { log }, the whole text.

--number, --top, --timeout and --poll are read as whole numbers from the start of the text, so 12abc is 12.

toil jenkins pipeline list --folder platform
toil jenkins --instance ephemeral pipeline list-runs --name platform/api-build --top 5
toil jenkins pipeline run --name api-build --parameter BRANCH=main --wait --allow-write

Settings at a glance

  • baseUrl required

    Jenkins server root, e.g. https://jenkins.imagile.dev

    TOIL_JENKINS_BASE_URL

  • username required

    Jenkins user name the API token belongs to

    TOIL_JENKINS_USERNAME

  • apiToken required secret

    Jenkins API token

    TOIL_JENKINS_API_TOKEN

  • instance

    The name --instance selects this connection by, when it isn't the connection's own name

    TOIL_JENKINS_INSTANCE

Commands at a glance

  • toil jenkinspipeline list

    List all jobs on the Jenkins instance (or within a folder)

    MCP jenkins_pipeline_list--folder <name>--instance <name>

  • toil jenkinspipeline get

    Get details for a specific job

    MCP jenkins_pipeline_get--name <job>--instance <name>

  • toil jenkinspipeline runwrite

    Trigger a build

    MCP jenkins_pipeline_run--name <job>--parameter <k=v>--wait--timeout <s>--poll <s>--instance <name>--allow-write

  • toil jenkinspipeline list-runs

    List recent builds for a job

    MCP jenkins_pipeline_list_runs--name <job>--top <n>--instance <name>

  • toil jenkinspipeline get-run

    Get details for a specific build

    MCP jenkins_pipeline_get_run--name <job>--number <n>--instance <name>

  • toil jenkinspipeline logs

    Fetch console log for a build (consider --output-file for large logs)

    MCP jenkins_pipeline_logs--name <job>--number <n>--instance <name>
